title.purpose: Card/subsection H3s, FAQ questions, ledger labels, button labels.

motion.name: instrument-settle

motion.name: reveal-fade

narrative.overview: The system reads like the technical documents this software replaces — aircraft maintenance manuals, aeronautical charts, type certificates: precise, information-dense, printed-paper authority rather than screen-native gloss. Every AI-MRO competitor defaults to dark-mode-plus-glow; this system goes the other way on purpose, because a light, chart-like surface is the more differentiated and more honest choice for software that lives or dies on regulatory trust. The personality is precise, not sterile; authoritative, not corporate-cold. Warmth comes from a warm-neutral (not blue-black, not stark white) canvas and from a single confident amber accent — instrument caution lighting, runway-edge lighting — used exactly where it earns attention and nowhere else. The explicit anti-reference is the site's own prior look: generic dark-mode SaaS with blue/purple gradients, glow orbs, and a badge-eyebrow over every heading.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper canvas and graphite ink, never pure white or pure black
One signature accent color (instrument amber), spent sparingly
Flat, border-first depth — zero shadows anywhere in the implementation
Small, sharp radii — nothing rounder than 8px
Hand-built SVG technical diagrams (not photography, not stock UI mockups) carry the "instrument panel" motif: corner-tick graticule frames, station-reference lines, mono-set data labels

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only saturated color in the system and is spent sparingly — button fill, small text/icon accents, thin diagram strokes. Never a large fill or background.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Canvas and ink are always warm-tinted (oklch hue 80), never literal #fff/#000. This is what keeps "paper" and "ink" reading as material rather than as a default light theme.

rules.name: The One Data Face Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono appears only where the content is genuinely data-shaped — an index, a station reference, a timestamp-style detail — never as decorative texture on ordinary copy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Zero shadows anywhere in the implementation. Depth is conveyed entirely by hairline borders and a single subtle surface-tone step, plus one deliberate full-contrast reversal (the dark footer panel). Confirmed as a durable rule.

rules.name: The Corner-Tick Signature
rules.body: The one recurring form motif beyond the radius scale: a graticule frame made of four short amber L-shaped corner brackets, drawn as raw SVG paths, appearing around each hand-built technical diagram. Use at deliberate moments on new diagram-shaped content, not as generic page decoration.

dos: Do keep amber to a single signature accent — button fill, small text/icon accents, thin diagram strokes.
Do use a hairline border or a chart-paper → chart-paper-raised tone step for depth, never a shadow.
Do keep radii at 8px or under; rounded-full only for genuinely circular elements.
Do build new supporting visuals as hand-drawn SVG technical diagrams in the established ink/amber/line-strong language, not photography or fake product-UI screenshots.
Do vary section vertical rhythm (py-16–py-28) rather than repeating one spacing value down the page.
Do wrap section heading blocks (not every card) in the Reveal component for the one scroll-entrance motion the system uses; skip it on the Hero, which must render immediately for LCP.
donts: Don't use amber as a section background, large fill, or "brand wash" — its rarity is the point.
Don't add a shadow anywhere; reach for a border or a tone step instead.

Don't use graphite-ink-faint for real page content at normal text size — it fails WCAG AA (3.72:1) outside the SVG-diagram exception. Use ink-muted for anything that's genuine content rather than decorative diagram dressing.
Don't add an eyebrow/preheading label above a heading — the prior version of this page did this on every section and it was removed as decorative filler.

Don't invent stats, testimonials, or certification badges — see PRODUCT.md's Evidence on Hand; the prior version of this page fabricated exactly this kind of proof and it was removed for being untrue.

Don't "fix" the nav logo chip's or the favicon's literal #1c1a17 / #dfa23a hex values into token references — both render through Satori (next/og's ImageResponse) or are hand-matched to it, and Satori does not support CSS custom properties or oklch().
